title: Filtered finite-free projection via bounded-below direct-image continuity
statement:
Let $f:X\to Y$ be a quasi-compact quasi-separated morphism of schemes [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], with small pro-etale sites in a coefficient universe [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-size-convention]. Let $R_Y$ be a sheaf of commutative rings, fix $R_X\cong f^{-1}R_Y$, and use sheaves of modules, ordinary unbounded derived categories and the canonical derived ringed adjunction $L=Lf_R^*\dashv G=Rf_{*,R}$ with counit $\varepsilon$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category, def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. Thus $L$ on degree-zero modules is exact inverse image. Use K-flat derived sheaf tensor and its canonical pullback comparison [def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product, lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback].

Let $I$ be a small nonempty filtered category [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], let $(P_i)$ be a diagram of finite free $R_Y$-module sheaves, and let $v_i:P_i\to B$ exhibit a colimit $B$ in $R_Y$-module sheaves. Assume $B$ and $LB$ are flat, where flat means that tensoring with the module is exact [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. Fix $C\in D^+(R_X)$ [def-weil-pbc-bounded-derived-subcategories] and $A=GC$. For any $R_Y$-module sheaf $P$, define
$$\delta_P:P\otimes^L_{R_Y}A\longrightarrow G(LP\otimes^L_{R_X}C)$$
to be the adjoint of the canonical pullback/tensor comparison followed by $1\otimes\varepsilon_C$ (with symmetry ordering the $P$ factor first).

Then $\delta_B$ is an isomorphism in $D(R_Y)$. More precisely, every $\delta_{P_i}$ is an isomorphism, identified under any finite free presentation $P_i\cong R_Y^{\oplus d_i}$ and its pullback with the finite-biproduct comparison $A^{\oplus d_i}\to G(C^{\oplus d_i})$. The actual cocone legs satisfy
$$\delta_B\circ(v_i\otimes1)=G(Lv_i\otimes1)\circ\delta_{P_i}.$$
For any representative $K^\bullet$ of $C$ vanishing below one integer $a$, the canonical map
$$\varinjlim_i H^qG(LP_i\otimes^L C)\xrightarrow{\sim}H^qG(LB\otimes^L C)$$
is an isomorphism for every $q$; it is induced by $G(Lv_i\otimes1)$ and the degreewise diagram $LP_i\otimes K^\bullet$. Under the leg-induced identification $H^q(B\otimes^L A)\cong\varinjlim_iH^q(P_i\otimes^L A)$, the map $H^q(\delta_B)$ is the colimit of $H^q(\delta_{P_i})$ followed by this continuity isomorphism. No assertion about unbounded filtered diagrams or infinite coproduct preservation is made.

proof.text: Compare any recorded tensor model to the native derived tensor using fully faithful whiskering on flat K-flat representatives [lem-weil-pbc-resolving-representative-whiskering, lem-pc-kflat-resolution, lem-sf-ringed-derived-native-tensor]. Consequently tensoring by a fixed object is additive and tensoring by the degree-zero unit is naturally isomorphic to the identity. The module pullback carries the unit to the unit [def-weil-pbc-projection-formula-arrows]. For the given canonical pullback comparison, naturality of adjuncts proves projection_naturality directly. For the unit, conjugate the tensor comparison by these two unit-action isomorphisms, obtaining a natural automorphism of L. Conjugacy under L ⊣ G gives an automorphism of G, so its component is invertible. Cancelling the target unit isomorphism shows that the actual projection at the unit is invertible. Choose the source unit identification as this projection followed by the target identification; this supplies exactly the existential unit normalization in the unchanged statement.

proof.text: Both coefficient functors are additive, hence preserve finite coproducts, and direct image is additive. For any specified finite-free presentation, precompose with every coproduct injection. Naturality of the actual projection identifies its component with the coproduct of the rank-one projections followed by the direct-image comparison. This is the required sigmaComparison identity, including empty rank. All its factors are invertible, so every finite-free projection is invertible.

source.place: Lemma 5.3(1), equation (5.4); agent finite-free projection and cocone assembly from returned proof steps 4-5

proof.text: For source cohomology, choose one flat-term K-flat resolution of a representative of GC [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. The native one-K-flat tensor comparison [lem-sf-ringed-derived-native-tensor], followed by comparison with the specified tensor model, identifies the source functor on coefficients with single(-) tensor that fixed complex followed by Q. Tensoring module sheaves preserves coefficient-sized colimits [lem-weil-pbc-independent-sheaf-tensor-colimits]; the existing complex bifunctor-colimit instances give the same for signed total tensor. Filtered colimits are exact because module sheaves are Grothendieck abelian [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist]. Homology preserves these exact colimits. Thus the mapped source cocone is colimiting, and its actual canonical desc is invertible. This argument needs no boundedness of GC and no flatness hypothesis on the varying coefficient.

source.place: Lemma 5.3(1), equation (5.4); agent finite-free projection and cocone assembly from returned proof steps 4-5

proof.text: Finite coproducts of the tensor unit are flat; pullback preserves coproducts as a left adjoint and takes the unit to the unit. Thus each pulled-back finite-free coefficient is flat. For any representative K of C with common lower bound n, flat_single_derived_normalization [lem-pur-flat-single-derived-normalization] makes single(LP) K-flat for each coefficient in the diagram and for its stated flat colimit. The native one-K-flat tensor comparison and the exact-pullback/single comparison identify the strict signed-total diagram with the derived tensorTarget diagram. Naturality of those comparisons proves the leg equation for every actual v_i. The single-factor total-tensor formula shows every term and the colimit vanish below n. Pullback, single and total tensor preserve colimits, so the strict mapped cocone is colimiting.

source.place: Lemma 5.3(1), equation (5.4); agent finite-free projection and cocone assembly from returned proof steps 4-5

proof.text: Apply bounded continuity with the actual coefficient action [lem-pe-bounded-continuity-coefficient-restriction] to this uniformly bounded strict diagram and its actual colimit cocone. It gives the displayed strict desc isomorphism for every such K and every q. Existence of a bounded strict representative follows from the standard t-structure [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category]. Transport its mapped colimit cocone through the tensor comparison and its proven leg equation. This proves that the actual target desc is invertible.

source.place: Lemma 5.3(1), equation (5.4); agent finite-free projection and cocone assembly from returned proof steps 4-5

proof.text: Naturality of the projection transformation and the universal property of colimits give the displayed equality between source desc followed by H^q(delta_B) and the colimit of the finite-free projections followed by target desc. Both desc maps are invertible by the preceding steps; every component of the intervening natural transformation is invertible by finite-free normalization. Hence H^q(delta_B) is invertible for every integer q. The unbounded derived-category isomorphism criterion DerivedCategory.isIso_iff now proves delta_B invertible, without a separate bounded-below direct-image preservation theorem.
